title: Sunny and the Dewdrop World
description: Little Sonny the quokka wakes early to find the whole bush covered in tiny glittering dewdrops. A sparkling, magical bedtime story for little ones. Part of Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
Sunny woke up earlier than usual, while the bush was still grey and quiet and cool.

He stepped outside and stopped.

The whole world was glittering.

Every blade of grass, every spider's web, every leaf and twig and curl of bark was covered in tiny drops of water. Hundreds. Thousands. Each one round and perfect, holding its own little piece of the sky.

Sunny walked very slowly, not wanting to disturb anything.

He bent down close to a spider's web strung between two low branches. The web was completely covered in dewdrops, each one perfectly spaced, and the whole thing looked like a tiny jewelled net hung just for him to find.

He didn't touch it.

He straightened up and looked at a single blade of grass with a large drop balanced on its very tip. Inside the drop, Sunny could see a tiny reflection of the whole morning — the grey sky, the dark trees, even a small smudgy version of himself, looking back.

Hello, he thought.

The drop held its shape for one long, perfect moment.

Then it tipped and fell and was gone.

Sunny stood in the middle of the dewdrop world as the sun began to come up behind the trees, turning every single drop to gold and pink and bright white light.

It lasted only a little while. Then the warmth came, and the drops evaporated one by one, and the world went back to being ordinary.

But Sunny kept the memory of it, bright and perfect, like a dewdrop in his heart.

Goodnight, little Sunny. Goodnight, glittering morning. Goodnight, tiny and perfect and gone.
